assumptions: The exact version-4 concept has no paid pilot, committed laboratory or consultant channel, validated price, renewal evidence, or granted reuse rights beyond what is stated in the packet.

Accredited laboratories remain the authority for testing, and a contracted competent water-safety professional signs interpretation, control decisions, and escalation; the product is evaluated only as workflow and evidence software.
The reported lodging-premises exceedance rate demonstrates that qualifying events exist but is not extrapolated to all hotels or treated as a validated annual case frequency for a target portfolio.
The optional annual subscription is not assumed to sell, and the per-case model is assessed as episodic until actual portfolio incidence and renewal data exist.
Research version 2 is treated as evidence about regulation, incidence, expert boundaries, and incumbent products, not as validation of the redesigned version-4 offer or economics.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: A laboratory-confirmed exceedance creates a concrete, urgent handoff from result to expert decision, remediation, retest, and audit evidence. Packaging that fragmented episode into one governed case record is coherent, but the packet does not establish that hotels currently lack this coordination rather than receiving it from consultants, laboratories, or existing Legionella software.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: The underlying pain is serious: exceedances carry health, operational, reputational, and compliance consequences, and official inspection evidence shows real failures in lodging premises. Hotels clearly spend on testing and remediation, yet incremental willingness to pay for a separate casebook is unknown and may be weak when an incumbent consultant or laboratory already coordinates the response.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: The staged secure-upload pilot and refusal to build connectors before demonstrated payback limit upfront capital risk. However, no price, case frequency, annual-contract conversion, gross margin, CAC, retention, or owner-earnings path is evidenced; sporadic case fees may not support acquisition, and expert review, support, insurance, and secure handling can consume contribution.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Multi-site hotel operators are a specific, operationally coherent beachhead with repeated properties and a common trigger. The evidence confirms relevant incidents but does not quantify reachable portfolios, qualifying cases per year, software spend, or the revenue capacity of this niche, so economic sufficiency for the founder's wealth objective remains uncertain.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Hotel-specific templates and a complete positive-to-retest record could support a focused niche position. Domination is unlikely without channel control because laboratories, competent consultants, facility systems, Eurofins-style portals, and specialist Legionella platforms already sit closer to the workflow and can bundle similar case management.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven hotel workflow could extend to healthcare, collective residences, other priority buildings, additional geographies, and adjacent water-safety evidence processes. Expansion is plausible but not automatic because each segment can require different expert relationships, controls, procurement, liability boundaries, and comparable-system data.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: The proposed data advantage depends simultaneously on explicit operator reuse rights, enough positive-to-retest cases, and meaningful comparability among heterogeneous systems, none of which is established. The workflow itself is readily copyable, while incumbent laboratories and specialist platforms have superior access to results, customers, and historical data.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A single expert-governed, audit-ready dossier may improve convenience, traceability, and portfolio oversight, and preserving accredited results and named expert authority is a sound trust design. There is no demonstrated improvement in response time, labor cost, compliance outcomes, insurance risk, or retest success large enough to force switching or add a separate budget line.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Persistent EU and Polish monitoring duties, frequent poor results, and rising reported disease burden support sustained attention to Legionella control. The regulations are established rather than a new adoption window, and the existence of mature portals and specialist platforms shows that the category has momentum but is not an uncontested opening.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: A direct secure-upload pilot is realistically testable without integration, and one multi-site operator could expose several properties. Repeatable acquisition is weakly specified: no referral commitment exists, consultants and laboratories may prefer their own tools, positive events are intermittent, and direct enterprise hotel selling remains founder-intensive.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A bounded pilot appears feasible within the stated capital and part-time schedule, and the explicit separation of testing and expert authority reduces a major category error. Execution still requires a credible expert, secure and reliable evidence handling, careful liability and controller-processor terms, urgent escalation design, manual data-quality work, and B2B sales; false reassurance would be a severe failure mode.

main_structural_strength: The offer attaches to a narrow, high-consequence, externally verified trigger and keeps accredited testing and competent control decisions outside the founder's authority, enabling a capital-light pilot around an auditable result-to-retest record.
primary_score_limiter: The concept has not shown that hotel operators will buy this coordination separately from laboratories, consultants, or facility systems at a price and frequency that covers acquisition, expert review, support, insurance, and secure operations; without that, neither recurring economics nor the data advantage works.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Laboratory portals and specialist Legionella platforms already advertise trend analysis, dashboards, and non-compliance management, while official guidance requires system-specific competent interpretation. Together, this indicates that the software layer is bundleable and substitutable and cannot itself deliver the decisive control outcome.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Run paid pilots across at least two independent multi-site hotel portfolios and document accepted case and annual prices, eligible-case incidence, sales cycle and acquisition effort, expert minutes, support and insurance cost, contribution and payback, renewal or expansion behavior, referral conversion, explicit reusable-data rights, and a measured reduction in response time, labor, documentation defects, or failed retests versus the incumbent process.
highest_value_structural_change: Make a minimum annual portfolio contract, rather than optional subscription or isolated case fees, the core unit and co-sell it with the operator's incumbent competent water-safety consultancy, bundling a defined number of cases and explicit outcome-reuse rights. This would align recurring revenue, qualified governance, distribution, and data capture, but should be adopted only after a paid pilot proves partner incentives and contribution.
